newsitem.title: UK: UK union set to make pledge to limit strikes - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK union set to make pledge to limit strikes - paper.

text.p: Britain's Trades Union Congress is set to make a pledge limiting strike action as part of an effort to reduce potential conflict with a future Labour government, said the Financial Times on Wednesday.
The report said this would be an unprecedented step by union leaders ahead of an election which must be held by May 22, with the opposition Labour Party riding high in the polls.
John Monks, TUC general secretary told the FT in an interview "We will try to avoid strikes and seek far greater involvement of third parties in conciliation and arbitration."
He added that the unions wished to create an agenda with employers to improve corporate performance through better training and increased investment.
He denied that unions were setting out a "shopping list" of demands and stated that the union movement could only survive if it stepped away from the traditional cosy relationship with Labour.
The views will be launched by the TUC on Wednesday in its document "Partners for Progress" which aims to ensure that unions will not be blamed if a future Labour government collapsed.

Strikes under the last Labour Government which ended in 1979 after the so-called "winter of discontent" of industrial action were partly blamed for toppling Labour from power. Labour has remained out of power since then.

"The background is that two out of the last three periods of Labour in office ended after disputes with unions," said Monks in the FT, referring to the above winter of discontent and a row over labour relations reform in 1969.
But he said the unions will be seeking measures for greater job security in the public sector and supporting a minimum hourly wage pitched at four stg.
The TUC would also like to see a task force involving unions, employers and the Bank of England to look at when it will be right to join a European single currency. --London newsroom +44 171 5427717
